title: Scene 1 — The Courtyard Lanterns at Dusk
content:
Under the ancient Baobab tree, lanterns flickered against the twilight. Awa stood motionless before the council of elders, her gaze unwavering despite the heavy silence pressing down upon the courtyard.

Elder Kofi cleared his throat, leaning forward on his carved stool. "Awa, daughter of Nkwanta, the bride-price has been settled. Chief Bawa has sent fifty bags of salt, twelve cattle, and royal cloths of gold. Why do your feet hesitate to cross his threshold?"

Awa lifted her chin, the red beads around her neck catching the lantern light. "Because, respected Elder, a marriage forged in coins and cattle without the consent of the heart is not a marriage—it is an auction. And my life is not livestock to be bartered in the evening market."

A gasp rippled through the gathered kin. Mother Efua gripped her wrap tightly, her eyes wide with terror and pride.

"You speak of rebellion!" Chief Bawa’s envoy roared, stepping into the center circle. "The customs of our ancestors cannot be rewritten by a defiant maiden!"

"If our ancestors lived today," Awa answered with steady calm, "they would weep to see custom weaponized to chain their daughters. If you want Chief Bawa’s wealth, return it yourself. My destiny belongs to God, to my people, and to myself."

With those words, the courtyard ignited into fierce debate. The old order had been shaken, and the voice of the village would never be silenced again.

title: Scene 2 — Challenging the Elders and the Oath
content:
=== SCENE 2 — CHALLENGING THE ELDERS AND THE OATH ===

Setting: the Royal Courtyard of Oguaa & the Market Square. The atmosphere is charged with tension.

Awa: "We have walked under this cloud long enough. If we do not speak now, the truth will be buried beneath the soil of our ancestors!"

Elder Kofi & Mother Efua: "Do you dare defy the council? Tradition was carved into stone long before your father learned to walk."

Awa: "Tradition that suffocates its own children is not wisdom—it is fear wearing a crown. Today, we choose life."

The onlookers murmur. The drumbeats slow, then erupt in a rhythmic cadence that reverberates across the hills.

Elder Kofi & Mother Efua: "Then let heaven be the judge between your conviction and our law."

With a decisive movement, Awa turns toward the gathered assembly. The stage dims to an amber glow as destiny shifts into motion.
